text:
maria: Heads up — saw a regression on staging when serving very long contexts with INT8. p95 latency climbed ~12% overnight, not in prod yet.
ajay: ugh. any traces/metrics? is it pure CPU/GPU or KV churn?
maria: perf-bot posted a snapshot. KV page-in and memcpy dominate during the spike.
perf-bot: snapshot 1987654380: kv_page_in 6.2k/s, kv_memcpy 72% gpu time, page-faults 8200/s, active_slots 1.8M.
lee: that rate of page-in looks like eviction thrash — we might be compacting too eagerly when quantized slots are smaller.
sofia: INT8 reduces slot size but increases slot count. fragmentation + allocator behavior could make reuse worse, not better.
ajay: can you share repro? I want to try toggling prefetch and eviction policy.
maria: repro command:

```
RUNTIME_FLAGS=\"--kv-quant=int8 --evict-threshold=0.85 --prefetch=on\"
./bin/loadgen --model redwood-medium --seq-len=32000 --batch=1 --qps=50
```

maria: with that, we see steady-state memory at ~48GB but frequent short-lived spikes where free slab pages drop and page-in skyrockets.
lee: I ran a short trace: kernel selection flips to non-fused attention during high mem pressure (fallback path). Matmul kernels also move from int8-fast to bf16-fallback intermittently.
ajay: interesting — kernel selector is observing degraded alignment and switching. That can add a few ms per token due to different kernel tiling.
sofia: so this is a coupling: quantization increases fragmentation -> evict/prefetch churn -> kernel selector sees layout/seq changes -> chooses slower kernels -> latency regresses.
maria: exactly.
lee: quick experiment idea: add wear-leveling prefetch sweep that prioritizes hot-slot coalescing before evicting. If we coalesce small INT8 slots into contiguous pages, memcpy cost should drop.
ajay: also try disabling aggressive prefetch for INT8 workloads. Prefetch helps cold-starts but might amplify thrash under longctx.
sofia: what about BF16 fallback policy? BF16 keeps fewer slots than FP16 but avoids int8 packing overhead. Maybe a hybrid policy: prefer BF16 when active_slots > N.
junior-infra-note: (bot) remember to tag kernel-bisect when running multiple builds.
maria: I ran a quick BF16 run — memory up 10% vs INT8 but p95 dropped back to baseline. Accuracy delta negligible for our QA prompts.
lee: profiling snippet from nvprof (short):

```
Time(%)  Name                Calls  Avg
72.3     kv_memcpy           1200   0.45ms
14.8     attention_fw        960    0.12ms
6.9      matmul_int8_fast    480    0.05ms
```

lee: when eviction thrash starts, kv_memcpy jumps to ~90% and matmul_int8_fast disappears.
ajay: action plan:
 - ajay: run kernel bisect (flash vs fused) under the same repro with and without prefetch (ETA 4h)
 - lee: prototype a coalescing prefetch sweep that tries to merge adjacent INT8 slots before eviction (ETA EOD)
 - sofia: run BF16 fallback comparisons across our eval prompts to check quality delta (ETA EOD)
 - maria: ramp staging load to 2x and collect traces for the above runs (ETA 2h)

maria: I'll attach the staging perf bundle after the runs. tagging @ajay @lee to sync later.
ajay: thanks. if bisect shows kernel selector flipping is the culprit we can gate selection on contiguous kv layout/frag metric.
sofia: good. also add a telemetry gauge for \"kv_frag_ratio\" so ops can see when INT8 is causing bad packing.
lee: note — coalescing will add CPU overhead during eviction; need to measure cost vs saved memcpy.
maria: agreed. small wins first: toggle prefetch and temp prefer BF16 for longctx customer tests.
perf-bot: created perf-issue-2487 linked to thread 1987654321 :warning:
maria: ok closing for now, will post results here when each run completes :rocket:
